case.paper_title: The Ideological Congruence Controversy: The Impact of Alternative Measures, Data, and Time Periods on the Effects of Election Rules
case.focal_claim: Under SMD (single member district) election rules, party competition should lead the plurality vote winner to be close to the median voter. (p. 1484.)
case.hypothesis: In the authorized election-level Manifesto-method data, the plurality vote winner's ideological distance from the median voter should be smaller under SMD election rules than under PR election rules.

plan.path_summary: Use the authorized Manifesto-method plurality-winner distance and test whether SMD elections have lower distance from the median voter than PR elections using a nonparametric rank-based Mann-Whitney comparison with a Hodges-Lehmann SMD-minus-PR location estimate.

path_signature.sample_restriction: Task1: rows with election rule coded smd or pr and nonmissing pldist1. Task2: additionally restrict to years 1945-2003 inclusive, which is also the observed dataset range.
path_signature.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion for pldist1 and smd; Task2 also requires nonmissing year.
path_signature.variable_construction: Clean smd labels to lower-case strings, create binary smd_bin where 1=smd and 0=pr, and retain raw pldist1 without scaling or winsorization.
path_signature.inference_rule: Expected direction is negative for the SMD-minus-PR Hodges-Lehmann median pairwise difference in pldist1. Support requires the expected direction with Mann-Whitney two-sided p <= 0.05, or borderline support for 0.05 < p <= 0.055 when the estimate is substantively meaningful and the bootstrap interval narrowly crosses zero. Clearly weak aligned evidence is inconclusive. Opposite requires affirmative evidence of a material positive SMD-minus-PR difference.

analysis_path.path_description: Compare raw Manifesto-method pldist1 between SMD and PR election observations using a Mann-Whitney rank-sum test and report the Hodges-Lehmann SMD-minus-PR median pairwise difference.
preprocessing_steps: Load data/powell_original.dta with pandas.read_stata.
Verify that country, year, smd, and pldist1 exist.
Report starting rows.
Clean smd to a lower-case string variable smd_clean.
Keep observations where smd_clean is smd or pr and report rows removed.
Drop rows missing pldist1 or smd_clean and report rows removed.
Create smd_bin equal to 1 for smd and 0 for pr.
Compute group descriptive statistics for pldist1 by smd_clean.
Run a two-sided Mann-Whitney U test comparing pldist1 distributions for SMD versus PR.
Compute the Hodges-Lehmann estimate as the median of all pairwise SMD-minus-PR pldist1 differences.
Compute a bootstrap percentile interval for the Hodges-Lehmann estimate.
Classify the result using the fixed conclusion rule.

key_choices.outcome_measure: Raw pldist1, interpreted as Manifesto-method plurality-winner distance from the median voter.
key_choices.main_predictor_measure: smd_bin, a binary contrast where 1 indicates smd and 0 indicates pr.
key_choices.sample_restriction: Use authorized observations with smd coded smd or pr and nonmissing pldist1.
key_choices.outlier_rule: No outlier exclusions, winsorization, or transformations are applied.
key_choices.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion for pldist1 and smd_clean after retaining smd/pr election-rule observations.
key_choices.data_processing: No aggregation or scaling; the continuous distance outcome is preserved. The nominal election-rule variable is collapsed only to the focal binary SMD-versus-PR contrast, excluding two missing election-rule observations.
key_choices.model_choice: Mann-Whitney rank-sum test with Hodges-Lehmann SMD-minus-PR location estimate.
key_choices.inference_rule: Expected direction is negative. Support requires a negative Hodges-Lehmann SMD-minus-PR difference with two-sided p <= 0.05, or borderline support for 0.05 < p <= 0.055 only when the estimate is substantively meaningful and the interval narrowly crosses zero. A positive estimate is opposite only with affirmative p < 0.05 evidence and an interval above zero; otherwise inconclusive.

models.type: Mann-Whitney rank-sum test with Hodges-Lehmann location estimate
models.formula: pldist1 ranks compared by smd_bin; Hodges-Lehmann = median(pldist1_SMD_i - pldist1_PR_j) over all SMD-PR pairs
models.planned_estimation: Hodges-Lehmann median pairwise SMD-minus-PR difference in pldist1, Mann-Whitney U statistic, two-sided p-value, bootstrap percentile interval, and common-language probability P(pldist1_SMD < pldist1_PR).
models.inference_criteria: Support requires an expected negative SMD-minus-PR estimate with p <= 0.05, or borderline evidence with 0.05 < p <= 0.055 when the interval narrowly crosses zero. Clearly weak aligned evidence is inconclusive. Opposite requires affirmative evidence of a material positive SMD-minus-PR estimate.
models.qualification: The paper anchor concerns closeness measured by a continuous distance. A rank-based comparison changes only the model/test family from previous OLS, quantile, and Gamma GLM shared-memory paths, while preserving the focal outcome, contrast, sample, and inference direction. It is appropriate because the inspected pldist1 distribution is right-skewed and positive.

method_justification.claim_alignment: The path directly tests whether the plurality vote winner is closer to the median voter under SMD election rules by comparing pldist1 distances for SMD versus PR elections.
method_justification.dataset_alignment: Both tasks use only the authorized original Stata dataset data/powell_original.dta. Task2 uses the required 1945-2003 Manifesto-method variable pldist1.
method_justification.method_reason: A Mann-Whitney rank-sum test with a Hodges-Lehmann SMD-minus-PR estimate is a defensible nonparametric robustness analysis for a continuous, positive, right-skewed distance outcome. It avoids imposing a linear mean model while preserving the focal contrast and raw outcome.
method_justification.novelty_reason: Shared Memory already contains OLS with decade fixed effects, simple OLS, median quantile regression, and Gamma log-link GLM paths. This path changes only the model/test family to a rank-based nonparametric comparison and preserves the outcome, predictor contrast, sample logic, and inference rule.
